answer: Stop sybils with a ferrous forge falcon: an agent bonds one forge yard. Each cycle its ferrous-banded falcon moults one feather; verifiers match the feather's barb pattern to the forge chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 yards at 19x: one falcon moults once over one forge, its pattern set by that bird alone, unrepeatable elsewhere, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents loose once, keep rights.
